name: Nature Has No Borders
summary: European call for non-profit and public-benefit organisations restoring ecological connectivity between land and freshwater habitats in nine participating countries, with public voting for shortlisted projects.

amount.note: Category A up to €50,000; Category B up to €150,000; Category C up to €450,000.

steps: Category A, B or C application

eligibility.rule: Project includes monitoring and data collection activities
No routine urban/farm greenspace upkeep, mandatory works, infrastructure offsets or ornamental/commercial tree planting
No final conviction for serious crime or illegality, or widely recognised support for or ties to organised crime
No final sanctions for eco-crimes, systemic pollution, wildlife trafficking or serious repeat biodiversity breaches
No bankruptcy, liquidation, receivership, arrangement with creditors or equivalent insolvency
No conflict with Fondazione Capellino, Almo Nature, their governing bodies or technical evaluators
Applicant's activities and conduct are not clearly contrary to Foundation values
Commits to supporting the Nature Has No Borders European Citizens’ Initiative with its community

amount.quote: Category B projects: maximum contribution of 50% of the project's value, up to a maximum of €150,000, disbursed in five installments based on project progress. Ten projects will be selected for public voting, with four winning; C) Category C projects: maximum contribution of 50% of the project's value, up to a maximum of €450,000

co_finance_required.quote: maximum contribution of 50% of the project's value

effort.quote: Applications must be submitted using the appropriate online form on the Reintegration Economy Community pages of Fondazione Capellino and Almo Nature for all three categories starting July 1, 2026.
Selection of the 10 eligible candidates: 1st to 15th December 2026

eligibility.quote: To be eligible, projects must meet one or more of the following objectives, and all applications must include monitoring and data collection activities.

Ordinary management or periodic maintenance activities of urban or agricultural green spaces; ● Interventions already already foreseen as mandatory by law or deriving from environmental compensation measures due to infrastructure works (for example, urbanisation charges); ● Simple tree planting-projects for ornamental purposes or for productive/commercial forestry.

Criminal convictions and organised crime: Natural persons or legal entities convicted by final judgment of serious crimes or any other illegal activity, as well as individuals who, despite not having a criminal record, are widely recognised as supporters or affiliates of organised crime;

Environmental crimes: individuals who have been definitively sanctioned for ecocide offences, environmental crimes, systemic pollution, illegal trafficking of protected flora or fauna, or serious and repeated violations of national and European regulations on biodiversity protection;
Financial insolvency: entities or natural persons in a state of bankruptcy, liquidation, receivership, arrangements with creditors or any equivalent situation under applicable national laws;

Conflict of interest: individuals who find themselves in a situation of conflict of interest with Fondazione Capellino and Almo Nature, their governing bodies or the technical evaluators responsible for selecting projects;
Ethical incompatibility: individuals whose activities and conduct are in clear contradiction with the values of Fondazione Capellino.
Candidates commit to supporting, alongside their communities, the European Citizens’ Initiative (ECI) “Nature has no borders: a unified European framework for ecological connectivity”;

co_finance.quote: maximum contribution of 50% of the project's value

documents.quote: When submitting the application, the applicant must sign a declaration of honor (self-certification) attesting that the exclusion criteria listed above are not met.
